tasks.short: Talk with clients or groups about education, childcare and problem solving, look up local services, put together information packets, and record the advice given.

steps.what: Community health worker advises clients or community groups on education, childcare or problem solving
Community health worker looks up local services to refer clients to
Community health worker puts together information packets by copying leaflets
Community health worker records the advice given in free text

tasks.design: A maintained social map of local services (childcare, schools, courses, debt help) is searchable by topic and neighbourhood ({OTHER}), so the worker does not search websites and folders. Information packets are printed from the selected entries with the vetted leaflets attached. Advice is recorded with a short template (topic, referral, next step). Advising stays with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Services were searched one by one and leaflets copied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Social maps can be kept as searchable lists that print packets.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a parent see a way out of a problem they have carried for years.

evidence.claim: A maintained list of local services can be searched by topic and print referral packets.
Client data that include health details are special category data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the client question to advice recorded; the service's own help is outside.
Input contract: the social map kept current; fallback is searching by hand.
research_questions: Do referrals reach the right service more often?

incremental.description: Community health worker reports outdated entries in the social map.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few referrals; high: many referrals to varied services.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the visit list and route, conduct home visits for pregnant women, newborns and high-risk individuals, fill the assessment checklist, and type the visit report into the record.

steps.what: Community health worker plans the visit list and route by hand
Community health worker conducts home visits to monitor progress of pregnant women and newborn infants
Community health worker fills the assessment checklist on paper
Community health worker types the visit report into the record at the office

tasks.design: The client record app on a tablet ({OTHER}) lists the day's due visits with addresses and orders them into a route, so the worker does not plan by hand. The assessment checklist is filled on the tablet during or after the visit and syncs to the record, so nothing is typed at the office. Visiting and assessing stay with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routes were planned by hand, checklists filled on paper and typed in later.
tasks.enabler_now: Client record apps run checklists on tablets and order visit lists into routes.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing that a new mother is not coping.

reach.learn: Whether visit findings are visible the same day.

evidence.claim: Client record apps can run checklists on tablets and sync them to the record.
Health records are kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from visits due to the record updated; referrals are outside.
Input contract: tablets for field workers; fallback is paper.
research_questions: Do findings reach the record the same day?

incremental.description: Community health worker syncs the tablet where there is no signal.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few visits a day; high: full visit rounds.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare parenting sessions and materials, teach parenting behaviours to families, and record attendance and progress.

steps.what: Community health worker prepares the parenting session and its materials
Community health worker teaches appropriate parenting behaviors to families
Community health worker records attendance and progress on paper

tasks.design: Vetted parenting materials are kept in a shared library by topic and child age ({DOCS}), so sessions are prepared from it instead of assembled each time. Attendance and progress are recorded on a short tablet form in the client record ({OTHER}). Teaching families stays with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials were assembled per session and progress kept on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared libraries and tablet forms are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Each family needs its own examples.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a tired parent a calmer way through bedtime.

evidence.claim: Shared libraries and tablet forms can hold vetted materials and session records.

assumptions: Boundary: from family needs to progress recorded; referral to therapy is outside.
Input contract: materials vetted by the team; fallback is own materials.
research_questions: Is preparation time per session shorter?

incremental.description: Community health worker suggests materials for the library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few sessions; high: regular group sessions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare health classes and adapt materials to the group's language and culture, arrange dates and venues, teach the classes, and record attendance and evaluations.

steps.what: Community health worker prepares health information and adapts it to the group's cultural norms
Community health worker arranges dates and venues with schools and groups by e-mail
Community health worker teaches classes on medical or dental health to school and community groups
Community health worker records attendance and paper evaluations

tasks.design: Vetted health materials are kept in a shared library in several languages, with pictures for low literacy ({DOCS}), so the worker adapts rather than makes them. Schools and groups pick a date from an online booking form instead of e-mail rounds. Attendance and a short evaluation are collected through a QR form at the end of the class. Teaching stays with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials were made per group, dates arranged by e-mail and evaluations collected on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared libraries, booking forms and QR forms are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Some languages have no vetted material.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining dental care in a way a family's grandmother accepts.

evidence.claim: Booking forms and QR evaluation forms are standard tools.

assumptions: Boundary: from the class request to the class recorded; the curriculum is outside.
Input contract: materials vetted by the team; fallback is own materials.
Schools book online in about the time an e-mail took; a little school time is priced.

incremental.description: Community health worker suggests materials in new languages.
Schools and groups book through the form.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few classes; high: regular school programs.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The community health worker keeps advising, visiting, teaching families and groups; service searches, paper checklists, typed reports and e-mail booking shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A worker with more time with families.
